purpose: Offline deterministic coverage matrix with exact provider-label audit. No runtime detector expansion, no model calls. Public network acquisition is a separate script.
authority: Detection routes are proposed project policy, not statements made by the source authors. No source identities are merged.
scope: 524 master source entries + 216 color-pie entries + 3 category pointers. Overlap is retained; these are not 740 unique mechanics.
limits: All 312 distinct direct-label candidates checked against the pinned complete Scryfall Oracle-card snapshot and three catalogs.
Direct means an exact reported-label route, conditional on the provider returning it. Missing metadata is unknown, not absence.
No percentage of cards covered, precision, recall or count of necessary card exceptions has been measured.
Rule profiles specify work to implement; they are not executable or validated Oracle recognizers.
Exception review includes undefined editorial scopes and opt-in domains; it does not mean each card needs manual mapping.
Inventory category/rules reference is not proof of current card legality. Color ownership never supplies card evidence.

supporting_evidence.role: full-corpus exact-label observations, counterexamples and sampled live consistency

endpoint_check.claim: Sampled consistency between the bulk snapshot and live collection endpoint; same provider, not independent validation.

limits: Observed labels are not proof of complete coverage or inherent possession; grants and reminder text need separate evidence.
No precision/recall estimate for semantic mechanics: no independently labeled full-card ground truth was supplied.
Catalog agreement supports provider terminology, not source category equivalence or card legality.
Color-pie-to-keyword semantic links beyond the original eight remain proposed even when a provider label is observed.
No runtime detector or discovery whitelist is expanded by this report.

source_variant_notes.text: **Landwalk**: islandwalk, swampwalk, mountainwalk, plainswalk, forestwalk, nonbasic landwalk, artifact landwalk, snow landwalk, etc.
**Protection**: protection from colors, multicolor, named cards, card types, subtypes, and other characteristics.
**Cycling**: basic typecycling and other typecycling variants.
**Partner**: Partner with [name], Choose a Background, and Doctor's companion variants.
**Start Your Engines!**: includes the Speed / Max speed framework.
**Venture into the Dungeon** includes Venture into [quality].
**Tap and Untap** is one CR entry covering both actions.
**Open an Attraction** and **Roll to Visit Your Attractions** belong to the Attraction framework.
**The Ring Tempts You** and **Face a Villainous Choice** are multiword keyword actions.
**Empower Jace** is a highly specific, set-specific action.

direct: Exact membership in a pinned provider keyword list. Preserve the returned string. Claim only provider-reported involvement; no possession, face, parameter, or completeness claim.
Require real provider fixtures for the label; test empty/missing keywords, case normalization, duplicate printings and card faces.
family_alias: Use an explicitly reviewed variant/alias table; preserve variant and parameter. Do not derive aliases by fuzzy matching or punctuation stripping.
Positive and negative fixtures for each approved variant; distinguish shared family names from unrelated same-name entries.
action: Parse the named action in an executable clause. Preserve actor, object, cost/effect role, conditions, quantities and zones. A word in a prohibition, trigger condition or reminder is a separate relationship.
Test performs / triggers on / prohibits / replaces / pays-as-cost / reminder-only uses; do not count all word occurrences as actions.
stat_modification: Parse signed power/toughness changes; preserve source type, affected objects, duration, one-shot versus ongoing and the exact source-label qualifiers.
Test each sign combination, team versus single targets, Auras versus spells/creatures, duration and counters versus direct stat changes.
characteristic_change: Parse explicit changes to type, color, land type or characteristics; preserve subject, duration and retained characteristics.
Test becoming versus already being a type, additions versus replacements, temporary versus persistent effects, and separate faces.
removal: Parse destroy/exile/sacrifice clauses and their target restrictions, controller, scope and linked return conditions. Preserve every restriction in the source label.
Test destroy versus exile, self versus opponent sacrifice, one versus all, power thresholds, compensation and delayed returns.
protection: Parse explicit prevention/prohibition or protection effects; preserve subject, target, duration and exceptions.
Test grants versus possesses versus removes, combat-only versus all damage, conditional versus unconditional and reminder-only text.
evasion: Parse attack/block requirements or restrictions with quantifiers, exceptions and duration; distinguish an ability from its removal or reference.
Test cannot block versus cannot be blocked, must attack versus may attack, one blocker versus all and granted effects.
win_condition: Parse explicit win/lose instructions or prohibitions, affected players and conditions. Never infer a strategy or a winning combination.
Test win versus cannot win, lose versus cannot lose, controller versus opponents, conditional triggers and replacement effects.
card_flow: Parse draw/discard/reveal/look/exile/play permissions as ordered clauses with zones, controller, duration and costs; preserve label-specific restrictions.
Test draw-then-discard versus discard-then-draw, optional actions, opponent draw, delayed permissions and cost versus effect.
graveyard: Parse exact source/destination zones, ownership, object restrictions and cast-versus-return actions; preserve label distinctions.
Test own versus any/opponent graveyard, hand versus battlefield destinations, exile actions and linked conditions.
copying: Parse copy effects with copied object, copy recipient, modifications and duration.
Test spell versus permanent copies, token copies, copy prevention, temporary versus permanent and cross-references.
control: Parse counter/restriction/tax clauses including target kind, payment, exceptions and controller.
Test counter a spell versus put a counter, abilities versus spells, unless payments, prohibitions and granted text.
combat: Parse damage/fight clauses with source, recipients, amount expressions and combat restrictions.
Test damage versus life loss, fight versus one-way damage, multiple targets, power-derived amounts and qualifying triggers.
sacrifice: Parse sacrifice/discard and cost boundaries; preserve actor, permitted objects, repeatability conditions and linked effects.
Test self-only sacrifice, another creature, forced opponent sacrifice, once-per-turn restrictions and death triggers.
disruption: Parse discard, mill, hand/library manipulation and choices with actor, zone, quantity and ordering.
Test costs versus effects, self versus opponents, optional choices, replacement effects and negated instructions.
life: Parse gain/lose/pay life with actor, quantity and cost/effect boundary; keep damage distinct.
Test each player versus you/opponents, paying versus losing, life-setting, replacement and linked gain/loss.
tempo: Parse tap/untap, bounce, blink, phase/turn and combat-step clauses; preserve objects, destination, timing and linked returns.
Test enters tapped versus tap action, next-untap restrictions, extra turns versus end turn, temporary exile and self-only effects.
theft: Parse control-changing clauses with controlled object/player, duration and follow-up conditions.
Test temporary versus indefinite control, exchanged control, player-turn control and merely referencing an opponent.
counters: Parse counter/token placement, removal, movement and replacement separately; preserve kind, quantity and recipient.
Test counterspell homonyms, token versus counter doubling, cost removal, references versus production and replacement effects.
mana: Parse mana production, land-play/zone movement and land-count conditions; preserve restrictions, duration and cost/effect role.
Test costs versus mana production, restricted spending, conditional production, additional land plays versus putting lands and permanent versus temporary sources.
rules_alteration: Parse a bounded registry of explicit permission/prohibition/replacement templates; keep unsupported wording unclassified.
Test scope, exceptions, timing, may versus cannot, replacement versus prevention and effects that grant rule text.
cheat_into_play: Parse hand-to-battlefield instructions and exact permitted card types, restrictions and payments.
Test from hand versus library/graveyard, put versus cast, optional payments, and permanent-type restrictions.
tokens: Parse token creation with kind, quantity, characteristics, controller and conditions; references to tokens are separate.
Test creates versus sacrifices/copies/references, replacement effects, variable numbers and named token definitions.
tutoring: Parse library searches with actor, permitted types, destination, reveal and shuffle requirements.
Test search versus top-N look, any card versus specific types, opponent searches, failure-to-find and prohibitions.
trigger: Parse a bounded trigger template with event, controller, qualifiers, frequency and resulting effect; record event and payoff separately.
Test triggers versus activation costs or effects, opponent versus own events, once-per-turn and multiple clauses.
state: Parse explicit references to the named state/resource and classify establishes / consumes / checks / changes. A decklist does not establish current game state.
Test gaining versus checking state, resource generation versus expenditure, starting-game instructions and negation.
modal: Parse explicit mode selection and bullet structure, choice counts, repeat permissions and additional costs.
Test modal choices versus reminder/list formatting and mutually exclusive versus repeatable choices.
numeric: Parse explicit numeric comparisons, X, mana-value references or characteristics; retain the measured object and comparison.
Test printed X versus variable effects, power versus mana value, thresholds, parity and hypothetical game-state values.
lookup: The supplied label does not establish a sufficiently precise executable definition. Add a reviewed definition first, then reusable rules or card-ID exceptions. No automatic card assignment.
Approved positive/negative examples and scope are required before activation. No similarity matching, color inference or generic catch-all.
special: Requires a separate scoped definition for digital, Acorn or historical behavior. Prefer reusable templates where supported; use card-ID exceptions only where necessary.
Validate domain and printing/Oracle revision; do not derive card legality from this category. Main supported scope must opt in explicitly.
unavailable: no supported released-card mapping in this inventory
Preserve the source entry as reference-only. Do not assign imported cards until a separately reviewed mapping is supplied.
No matches by default; test that identical words in unrelated card text do not activate the entry.
index: This is a category-index pointer, not a mechanic. Retain it for source completeness and never activate a mechanic display from it.
Exactly three playtest category pointers remain separate from the 524 named entries.

card_faces.name: Mishra's Manufactory
card_faces.oracle_text:
2-4 players | 2-4 packs | 10 min
OBJECTIVE:
Take on the role of one of Mishra's assembly workers and assemble the best invention from the mishmash of parts streaming down the conveyor belt. Strategically collect cards based on their color to win.
GET READY:
Open one booster for each player, remove all cards without _Magic_ card backs, and shuffle the rest together. Reveal four cards in a row stretching from the deck. These form the *conveyor belt*. The two cards closest to the deck are at the *back of the line* and the other two cards are at the *front*. Randomly determine who goes first.
LET'S PLAY:
On their turn, each player drafts one card from the conveyor belt. The two cards at the front of the line are free, but a player must discard a card they've already collected to draft a card from the back of the

card_faces.name: Mishra's Manufactory (cont'd)
card_faces.oracle_text:
line. Cards then slide forward to fill in the gap, and a card from the deck is added to the back of the line. Drafted cards are kept face up in front of each player, grouped by color (including colorless.) Play then passes clockwise.
Lands are wild (they count as any color, including colorless), and a multicolored card can be any of its colors. When you draft a wild or multicolored card, declare its color and place it in the corresponding group.
TO WIN:
The game ends when all cards have been collected. For each color, the player with the largest group of cards of that color gets *3 points*, and the player with the second largest group gets *2 points*. The card with the highest mana value breaks ties. If there is still a tie, each tied player gets half the points, rounded up.
Players also earn points for the number of groups they've collected: four groups = *2 points*, five groups = *4 points*, six groups = *6 points*.
The player with the most points wins!

card_faces.name: Urza's Blueprints (minigame)
card_faces.oracle_text:
2+ players | 2+ packs | 10 min
OBJECTIVE:
You've unearthed Urza's ancient blueprints for his Power Plant, Tower, and Mine! Race your fellow artificers to assemble all three iconic locations.
GET READY:
Open a booster for each player and remove any cards without _Magic_ card backs. Shuffle the remaining cards into a deck and deal five cards to each player. Randomly determine who goes first.
LET'S PLAY:
On each player's turn, they draw a card, then discard a card face up. Players may draw either the top card of the deck or the top card of the discard pile. If there are no cards left in the deck when a player tries to draw, shuffle the discard pile to form a new deck.

card_faces.name: Urza's Blueprints (cont'd)
card_faces.oracle_text:
After discarding, if a player has all the cards required for a new location (see below), they may reveal those cards and note they have constructed their version of that location. They must then discard all cards in their hand and draw a new hand of five cards. Play then passes to the next player.
Foils are wild and can cont as any color, mana value, or card type.
TO WIN:
The first player to construct all three locations wins!
THE LOCATIONS:
*Mine:* Requires five cards with different card types. (Creature, artifact, land, etc.)
*Power Plant:* Requires one card of each color. (White, blue, black, red, and green. Multicolored cards count as one color of your choice. Lands are colorless.)
*Tower:* Requires five cards with different mana values. (Lands have mana value 0.)

card_faces.name: Booster Sleuth
card_faces.oracle_text:
2 players | 2 packs | 10 minutes
OBJECTIVE:
Unlike Jace, not all of us can rely on telepathy to solve a mystery. Using other cards as clues, discover all the facts about your opponent's mystery card.
GET READY:
Randomly determine who goes first—that player is the Secretkeeper, and their opponent is the Detective. First, the Secretkeeper opens a pack and removes any lands and cards without Magic card backs. Next, they shuffle the remaining cards and pick one at random. That card is the mystery card. Finally, the Secretkeeper gives the Detective the rest of the cards, and the game begins.
LET'S PLAY:
The Detective must correctly guess four facts

card_faces.name: Booster Sleuth (cont'd)
card_faces.oracle_text:
about the mystery card: converted mana cost, color, card type, and the number of words in its name. To do this, they choose and reveal cards one at a time.
When each card is revealed, the Secretkeeper tells the Detective how many of the four facts that card and the mystery card have in common. Then the Detective may either guess the four facts or reveal another card to get more clues.
The Detective gets only one guess, and they must guess all four facts correctly to win. Once the Detective has guessed, the round ends and the players switch roles with a new pack.
TO WIN:
Discover all four facts using as few cards as possible. The Detective who guesses correctly using the fewest clue cards wins! If neither player guessed correctly, or if there is a tie, play another round!

card_faces.name: Strictly Better
card_faces.oracle_text:
3-6 players | 3-6 packs | 15 minutes
OBJECTIVE:
Some cards are strong in Standard, others shine in Draft, but which card looks the tastiest? Take turns being the Judge and decide which Magic card is the best of the best in each wacky category.
GET READY:
Randomly determine who will be the first Judge. Each player then opens a pack, removes any cards without Magic backs, and looks at their cards.
LET'S PLAY:
The Judge chooses a category from the list on the back of this card (either their favorite or at random). The other players each secretly submit a card from their pack that they think fits the category.
When the Judge has collected all the cards, they reveal each card, read it aloud, then choose the winner.
The Judge role then passes to the next player, and they select a different category.

rows.name: Card draw
rows.source_explanation: Blue is best at card drawing. It has the most of it and no restrictions. Black's card drawing must involve paying some other cost, most often life but sometimes sacrificing permanents. Green's card draw is tied to creatures. In the past, we've also connected it to land, but that ended up making green card draw a little too much like blue, so we've pulled back from that. All colors get cantrips (spells that draw you a single card). Blue gets the best cantrip spells, white gets the best cantrip small creatures, and green gets the best cantrip large creatures. While white is still tertiary at card drawing, we have added some new abilities for white to draw cards. The big limitation is that white tends to draw over time rather than all at once, so it has a once-per-turn limit on card drawing (multiplayer does allow white on occasion to draw multiple cards tied to how many opponents a player has). Other than cantrips, red only draws cards with three exceptions: impulsive draw, "punisher" effects, and wheeling. (See impulsive draw, "punisher" effects, and wheeling.)

rows.name: Flash
rows.source_explanation: Everyone gets some access to flash. Blue gets it the most as it plays into the color's reactive play style. In the last few years, we made it secondary in white and black, and kept it secondary in green. White tends to get the small cheap and mid-size defensive creatures, black gets creatures that can surprise kill you, often with higher power than toughness, and green gets bigger creatures. Red can get flash when it functionally needs it to get an effect to work, most often with reactive enters-the-battlefield effects.

rows.name: "Transformation" (Target creature becomes a (color) (card type) with N power and N toughness.)
rows.source_explanation: Transformation can be temporary, through a one-shot spell that lasts for the turn, or more permanent, usually through an Aura. It overwrites the base power and toughness of the creature. This ability used to be in both blue and white, but we decided to focus it in blue. Sometimes blue can overwrite what the creature is currently doing and just make it the "transformed" creature. The one thing that we've taken from blue is destroying or exiling a creature and then giving the controller of that creature a creature token as a means of flavoring transformation. That is now a white ability flavored as giving compensation for destroying/exiling the creature. This means all of blue's transformation abilities are auras or limited effects on spells or activations.

rows.source_explanation: Ever since the card [autocard mvid="45235"]Twiddle appeared in Limited Edition (Alpha), blue has had the ability to tap or untap permanents. rows.name: Untapping creatures
rows.source_explanation: Untapping creatures used to be white's domain, but we moved individual creature untapping off to green to give it more creature answers. White still can untap all your creatures or an individual creature on a spell that's defined as solely defensive. Blue's ability to untap is usually accompanied by its ability to also tap (see twiddle above).

rows.name: Vigilance
rows.source_explanation: White tends to get this on creatures where the power is equal to or less than the toughness, and seldom with a power greater than 3. Green tends to get this ability on larger creatures to differentiate it from white. We've recently decided to also make blue secondary in vigilance because we were looking for more creature abilities to use in blue. We're still feeling out what kind of blue creatures will get vigilance.

rows.name: Ward (for mana)
rows.source_explanation: Ward is a new evergreen ability. It makes any opponent who wishes to target the item with ward pay an additional cost. The most common way we use this is ward for mana, and that's in white, blue and green. It's in white because it's both the most protective and taxing color; and it's in blue and green, flavored as antimagic, in places where hexproof used to be.

rows.source_explanation: This ability started in red with Keldon Warlord in Limited Edition (Alpha). We later moved it into green, as green is the creature color. The ability then got moved into white because white is the army color that likes giving rewards for having lots of little creatures. We still do the ability a little in green, but it's mostly in white these days.

rows.name: "Wheeling" (All players discard their hand and draw N cards.)
rows.source_explanation: There's a big debate in R&D as to whether this is supposed to be a red ability. It obviously goes all the way back to Limited Edition (Alpha) with Wheel of Fortune, but it's a raw form of card advantage that's supposed to be something red is bad at. For now, it stays in red's part of the color pie.
